Reason for the exceptions: already released earlier in the same unbroken cold spell, cannot release again until a thaw of roughly 40 F lets it creep back.
Reason 1: no locomotive in the 1962 dry bed.
Reason 2: the contemporaneous 8 March 1898 notice and CVR records — nobody died, derailed on land at the north approach.
Reason 3: Tolliver's own ledgers — 1901 purchase, 27 years, 1929 scrapping.
Each reason attributed to a named narrator or document, drawn from three different sources (highway engineer's survey; clerk's ledger plus newspaper; lumber company's books).
Independence argued explicitly (different record-keepers with no occasion to consult one another), and reasons 2 and 3 are each said to predate and survive the absence of the 1962 survey.
